25.text: In hunting from boats, the harpoon is thrown at the animal,

26.text: and the shaft becomes detached from the point in the same way as described.

27.text: Then the animal is hauled in, and the floating shaft picked up. At present,

28.text: however, seals do not allow the boat to come near enough for the use of the

29.text: harpoon. With the rifle they are shot at wherever they come out of the

30.text: water, no matter how far away they may be. The native hunters are pretty

31.text: good marksmen, but of course many shots go amiss. The animals that have

32.text: been killed sink so rapidly that they are often lost before the hunter can

36.text: Hunting on open water is more successful early in the season, when the

37.text: drift-ice is abundant, because all kinds of sea-animals go along with it, basking

38.text: all the while on its surface. Later on, when the ice has drifted away, the

39.text: animals become more scarce and the hunt difficult. Then the seal-hunters go

40.text: far out to sea in search of game. The Arctic hunters in their large boats

41.text: sail off with fair wind, and go so far that the highest mountain-tops near the

42.text: shore are out of sight. They remain in the open sea for two or three days,

43.text: waiting for a change of wind to get back to land.
